199cf0e42d.why: Echo fixed: 'rugged country' shares no word with the key, and 'rugged' fits the valley-floor lure as well as the ridges. Key true (USGS: ridges and hills that separate two watersheds are the divide; Grokipedia: typically a ridge, hill or line of high ground). No lower tier asks about divides. Voice clean.

873397d34b.why: The turbine lure is gone. 'Dissolved it in the lake's still water' is a real settling-versus-dissolving mix-up and is truly wrong (sand and mud settle; they do not dissolve). Two choices now name the lake, so the key no longer stands out by echo. Facts unchanged and sourced (reservoirs trap most of their inflowing sediment; Lake Nasser holds over 95 percent of the Nile's; the delta's coast retreated faster after 1970). It builds on T1's delta and sediment questions (a0d9a93aaa, 792f9e4c22) as a premise and keys the dam's effect, which is T3 human-impact content (MS-ESS3-3), not a re-ask.

32ef8ee88d.why: Echo fixed: 'thick, loose sediment' leaves the key to bring in clay. The 'pumped' echo is now shared by the cavern lure. The new lures are live and truly wrong: caverns form in limestone, not in loose sediment; the Dust Bowl's wind stripped about five inches (13 cm) of topsoil, not metres; the subsidence was not caused by fault movement. Key true: USGS says the cause is compaction of the aquifer system as pore water drains from the clay. The stem's numbers hold (USGS: as much as 28 feet, 8.5 m, by 1970). Grokipedia confirms the Dust Bowl line in the context (five inches from 10 million acres by 1938).

fa6dddf1c6.why: Both fact problems are fixed. The context's tide line is now true (tidal currents swing back and forth). The stem's nets are now lost at sea (Wikipedia: nets are nearly half the patch's mass, and debris comes from fishing vessels at sea). Key unchanged and true (NOAA: gyres pull debris to their centres). A minor point, not a fail: nets lost far out make the coast-based tide and wave lures a little easier to strike, but neither ever gathered rubbish into one spot, and the ship-dumping lure stays live. Coriolis is named only in the context (T4's ground), and the context's plastic bits do not re-key T1 7d3ffac908.

451aa02fef.why: New fact, sourced. EPA says wetlands work as natural sponges, and their storage and braking action lowers flood heights. EPA also says the Mississippi's bottomland wetlands once stored at least 60 days of floodwater and now store only 12, because most have been filled or drained, which matches the context. The key is a prediction, and the three lures are real beliefs: the water was drained off, the crops drink the rain, and the same rain makes the same flood. 'Most likely' covers the honest caveat. This is not T1 0235a0d2ac's paving and runoff fact (here the marsh stores water and lets it out slowly, which is not about soaking in), nor T2's terraces. Small style point: 'rise ... Lower' reads a little oddly but is clear.
